title: Boss: beat the clock
summary: Four problems with huge inputs: only the right Big-O finishes in time.

steps.title: The clock is the referee
body: Every run here is stopped after a few seconds of CPU time. A modern machine does a few hundred million simple steps a second, so:
| n | O(n) | O(n log n) | O(n²) |
Each challenge below is tested with inputs big enough that only an `O(n)` (or better) answer survives.

steps.title: The missing number
prompt: An array holds every number from `0` to `n` **except one**, in any order, so it has length `n`. Write `int Missing(int[] a)` that returns the missing number.
Aim for `O(n)` time and `O(1)` extra space. The tests use a million numbers.
Big hint: you know what `0 + 1 + ... + n` adds up to.
solution: foreach (var x in a) actual += x;
template: for (int dojoI = 0, dojoV = 0; dojoI < dojoBig.Length; dojoI++, dojoV++) { if (dojoV == 123_456) dojoV++; dojoBig[dojoBig.Length - 1 - dojoI] = dojoV; }
hints: Subtract the actual sum from the expected sum. Use `long`: a million numbers add up to more than `int.MaxValue`.

steps.title: First repeat
prompt: Write `int FirstRepeat(int[] a)`: the first value that appears for a **second** time as you read left to right, or `-1` if every value is unique. Values are between 0 and 999,999.
The tests include 1,000,000 distinct values, so you need one pass with a lookup table.
template: for (var dojoI = 0; dojoI < dojoBig.Length; dojoI++) dojoBig[dojoI] = (int)((dojoI * 7919L) % 1_000_000);
Dojo.Eq("a million distinct values gives -1", -1, FirstRepeat(dojoBig));
Dojo.Eq("a repeat at the very end is found", dojoBig[3], FirstRepeat(dojoBig));
hints: A `bool[]` with one slot per possible value: `new bool[1_000_000]`.
For each `x`: if `seen[x]` is already true, return `x`; otherwise set it.

steps.title: Doublings
prompt: Start with 1 and keep doubling. Write `int Doublings(long target)`: how many doublings until the value is **at least** `target`.
The tests ask for targets up to 10¹⁸, which is `O(log n)` steps for a doubling loop and far too many for counting up one at a time. No `Math.Log`.
hints: Use a `long value = 1` and double it in a `while (value < target)` loop.
Count each doubling; `int` for the value would overflow long before 10¹⁸.

steps.title: Balanced split
prompt: Write `int BestSplit(int[] a)`: choose a cut position `k` (from 1 to `a.Length - 1`) so that `|sum(a[0..k)) - sum(a[k..])|` is as small as possible, and return that smallest difference. The array has at least two items.
Summing both sides afresh for every cut is `O(n²)`. With 500,000 items you need `O(n)`: compute the total once, then slide the cut and keep a running left sum.
solution: foreach (var x in a) total += x;
template: for (var dojoI = 0; dojoI < dojoBig.Length; dojoI++) dojoBig[dojoI] = 1;
Dojo.Eq("500,000 items finish in time", 1, BestSplit(dojoBig));
hints: First loop: `total`. Second loop: add `a[k - 1]` to `left`; the right side is `total - left`.
Track the smallest `Math.Abs(left - (total - left))`. Use `long` for the sums.
